fields.h1: Build a Psychographic Questionnaire That Finds Your Segments
fields.hero_description: Build a psychographic questionnaire that scores each set of answers into a segment and saves it to the respondent's record.
fields.features_heading: Questions That Score Themselves Into Segments
fields.features_subheading: A list of good questions is half the job. Emergent builds the questionnaire and the scoring that reads its answers.
fields.feature_1:
Statements scored toward a segment

Tag each agree-or-disagree statement with the segment it points to. A person's answers add up per segment, and the segment with the highest total is saved on their record.
fields.feature_2:
Ranking questions for what matters most

Ask people to put five reasons they buy in order. The app counts first-place picks across every response and shows which value leads before anyone writes a campaign.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

A long run of statements reads better one at a time. Emergent can build the questionnaire as a conversational flow, with a single question per screen and a progress bar.
fields.feature_4:
Answers stored next to the person

Every response is a row in a database you own, tied to the person who gave it. Filter by segment, compare this quarter with the one before, or hand the table to an analyst.
fields.feature_5:
Segments sent to Slack and your CRM

Post a Slack message whenever someone lands in a segment you care about, or send each segment to your CRM through its API. The next email can then speak to that reader.
fields.feature_6:
Code export to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the full questionnaire app to your GitHub repository. A developer can then host it on your own servers and keep extending the scoring logic there.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Ways to Use the Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
Each of 412 buyers lands in one of 4 segments

Tansybrook Outfitters asks why campers buy its tents. Past buyers rate 12 statements on a 5-point scale, such as "I plan trips months ahead," and each adds points to a segment. The highest total wins. Of 412 buyers, the app tags 148 Trail Purists, 121 Weekend Families, 89 Gear Collectors, and 54 Budget Campers.
fields.tab_content_2:
Of 240 readers, 96 buy for where the tea grows

Juniperhall Tea hired Thistleby Studio to learn what its newsletter readers value before a spring campaign. Each reader ranks five reasons they buy tea. Origin came first for 96 of the 240 and flavor for 71, while price, health, and gifting shared the other 73. The studio wrote the campaign around the farms.
fields.tab_content_3:
Early adopters reach #beta-recruits after one answer

Glimmerwick, a note-taking app, asks each new signup how they take up new tools. Anyone who picks "I try new features the day they ship" is tagged as an early adopter and posted to #beta-recruits in Slack. This week 64 of 310 signups picked it, and product manager Isidro Verhoeven invited them to test offline sync.
fields.tab_content_4:
Before her first session, Thandiwe has a coach

Thandiwe Delaney joins Rook Hill Strength and fills in the intake questionnaire on her phone. She is training for a half marathon in May and wants a coach who pushes hard. The app matches those answers to Henrike Szabo, the coach who runs race training, and emails Henrike her profile ahead of their 6:30 a.m. session.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Psychographic Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan, score and build a psychographic questionnaire whose answers sort people into segments you can act on.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the decision the answers feed
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Pick four or five segments first
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Score each statement for a segment
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what changes once you know a person's segment: the email they get, the product page they see, or the coach they meet. A question that cannot change one of those decisions comes out of the questionnaire.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the segments before you write a single question, and give each one a sentence that describes the person in it. Four or five segments are enough to act on, and each still holds enough people to plan a campaign around.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write statements about what people value, how they spend free time and how they feel about your category. Split any statement that holds two ideas: "I plan trips and buy gear early" becomes two separate statements.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Link every statement to the one segment it describes and decide how the 5-point scale turns into points. Set a tiebreak rule before any response comes in, such as the segment with the most "strongly agree" answers.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add a ranking and an open question
fields.howto_step_5_des: A ranking question shows priorities that agree scales hide, because nobody can rate everything a 5. End with one open question, such as what they would miss if your brand disappeared, and read those answers by segment.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Put the statements, the segments, the scoring rule, and where results should go into one prompt. Emergent builds the questionnaire, the scoring and the database behind it, and you change any part by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send it to 20 people before you send it to 2,000. If one segment collects nearly everyone, or every respondent gives a statement the same answer, rewrite that statement and test it again before the full send goes out.
fields.hero_prompt: Build a psychographic questionnaire for my outdoor gear customers that asks how they spend weekends and what they value in a brand.

faq_plan.a: A psychographic questionnaire is a set of questions about how people think and live, not who they are on paper. It asks about lifestyle habits, values, and attitudes, the attributes psychographics describes, and the answers group respondents into segments a brand can market to.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a psychographic questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Decide which segments you want to find, write agree-or-disagree statements that point to each one, and set a rule that turns answers into a segment. With Emergent's AI form builder, you describe all of that in one prompt and get back the form, its scoring logic, and a table of responses.

faq_plan.q: How is a psychographic questionnaire used for segmentation?
faq_plan.a: It gives segmentation its raw material. Psychographic segmentation divides a market by personality traits, lifestyles, interests, attitudes, and values instead of age, income, or location. The questionnaire collects those answers one respondent at a time and scores each person into a group.

faq_plan.q: What topics should a psychographic questionnaire cover?
faq_plan.a: Cover values, interests, attitudes toward your category, and what drives a purchase. Tie interest questions to buying: a favorite things questionnaire asks what someone likes so a friend can pick a gift, while a psychographic one asks why those likes shape what they buy.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a psychographic questionnaire have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it near 12 statements, enough to score four segments with three statements each, and cut anything that does not feed a segment score. A one-question-per-screen layout, which Emergent can build, keeps a longer set readable on a phone.

faq_plan.q: How is a psychographic questionnaire different from a demographic one?
faq_plan.a: A demographic questionnaire asks who someone is: age, income, location, job. A psychographic one asks why they act, such as what they value and how they feel about a category. Ask both in one questionnaire and you can see whether the segment that ranks origin first also skews older.

faq_plan.q: Which question types work best in a psychographic questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Agree-or-disagree statements on a 5-point scale do most of the work, because they score cleanly. Add a ranking question for priorities and one open question for language you can reuse in copy. A wedding photography questionnaire uses open questions the same way, letting a couple describe the day in their own words.

faq_plan.q: How do I score a psychographic questionnaire into segments?
faq_plan.a: Assign each statement to one segment, convert each answer to points, with strongly agree as 5 and strongly disagree as 1, and add the points per segment. Whichever segment totals the most points is the respondent's. In an app Emergent builds, that rule runs on every response and the result lands in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Can I add a short psychographic questionnaire to a signup flow?
faq_plan.a: Yes, and keep it short. One question at signup is enough to tag an account, such as how someone takes up new tools. Save the full questionnaire for later, when the person has a reason to spend five minutes on it. The app can also push each tag into a CRM through its API.

faq_plan.q: What is an example question for a psychographic questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: "I would pay more for a product made close to home," rated on a 5-point agree scale, is one: it measures a value, not a fact about the person. An interior design questionnaire asks a version of the same thing when it asks which room photo feels most like home.

plan.angle: The top 10 is marketing explainers and question lists (Contentsquare, Alchemer, Sogolytics, Pollfish, a UNC library guide, Crazy Egg) and an AI Overview of sample questions: every result tells a marketer what to ask, and none builds the questionnaire or does anything with the answers. This page builds a psychographic questionnaire whose answers are scored into segments as they arrive, saved on each respondent's record, and used: a segment count for a brand, a ranked values chart for an agency, a Slack post for a product team, a coach match for a gym.
